questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward at $15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. One second later, another is thrown upward from the same point at $25\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. If $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, at what height do they meet?
questions.solution:
Taking $t$ from the first throw, the heights are $y_1=15t-5t^2$ and $y_2=25(t-1)-5(t-1)^2$.
$$y_1=y_2\Rightarrow t=1.5\text{ s},\qquad y=15(1.5)-5(1.5)^2=11.25\text{ m}$$

questions.stem: A car decelerates uniformly to rest after travelling $80$ m. If it covers the last $40$ m in $4$ s, what is its total stopping time?
questions.solution: For the last $4$ s, the car comes to rest, so $40=\frac12 a(4)^2$, giving $a=5\,\text{m s}^{-2}$$.\nFor$ the full stopping distance, $80=\frac12 aT^2$, hence $T=\sqrt{\frac{160}{5}}=4\sqrt2\,\text{s}$.

questions.stem: Two protons separated by a distance $r$ repel with a force of $3.0\times10^{-8}$ N. What is the repulsive force between two $\alpha$ particles separated by the same distance?
questions.solution:
By Coulomb’s law, at fixed separation $F\propto q_1q_2$. Each $\alpha$ particle has charge $+2e$, so
$$F_{\alpha\alpha}=4F_{pp}=4(3.0\times10^{-8})=1.2\times10^{-7}\,\text{N}.$$

questions.stem: A body starts from rest and moves with constant acceleration $2$ m s$^{-2}$. What distance does it travel during the fourth second?
questions.solution:
For motion from rest with constant acceleration, $s(t)=\frac{1}{2}at^2$. Thus, the distance during the fourth second is
$$s(4)-s(3)=\frac{1}{2}(2)(4^2-3^2)=7\text{ m}.$$

questions.stem: An electron and a proton, initially at rest, each gain the same kinetic energy in an accelerator. If $m_p/m_e=1840$, what is the ratio of the proton’s de Broglie wavelength to the electron’s?
questions.solution:
For a particle with kinetic energy $K$, $4\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$.
Since $K_p=K_e$,
$$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_e}{m_p}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1840}}.$$

questions.stem: A projectile is launched from level ground and lands at the same level. Its range is $60$ m and its maximum height is $20$ m. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, its launch speed and angle of projection are
questions.solution:
From $H=\dfrac{u_y^2}{2g}$, $u_y=\sqrt{2gH}=20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. Thus $T=\dfrac{2u_y}{g}=4\,\text{s}$ and $u_x=\dfrac{R}{T}=15\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.\\
$$u=\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2}=25\,\text{m s}^{-1},\qquad \theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{u_y}{u_x}\right)=53.1^\circ.$$

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and descends through a vertical height of $5$ m along a frictionless curved track. It then crosses a horizontal rough stretch whose first $4$ m has coefficient of friction $0.25$, followed by a portion with coefficient $0.5$. Taking $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, how far from the start of the rough stretch does it stop?
questions.solution:
By conservation of energy, the kinetic energy per unit mass at the rough stretch is $gh=10(5)=50\,\text{J kg}^{-1}$. The first $4$ m dissipates $\mu g d=0.25(10)(4)=10\,\text{J kg}^{-1}$, leaving $40\,\text{J kg}^{-1}$.
$$d_2=\frac{40}{0.5(10)}=8\,\text{m},\qquad d=4+8=12\,\text{m}.$$

questions.stem: Rain falls vertically at $6$ m s$^{-1}$. A man walks horizontally at $2$ m s$^{-1}$ and holds his umbrella tilted at angle $\theta$ to the vertical. If he doubles his speed without changing the rain, by what factor does $\tan\theta$ change?
questions.solution:
The umbrella aligns with the rain’s velocity relative to the man, so $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v_{\text{man}}}{v_{\text{rain}}}$. Since the rain speed is unchanged, doubling the man’s speed doubles $\tan\theta$.
$$\text{Factor change}=2$$

questions.stem: In a Young's double-slit experiment, narrowing one slit makes the wave amplitude from it half that from the other slit. The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is
questions.solution:
For amplitudes $A_1=2a$ and $A_2=a$, $I_{\max}=(A_1+A_2)^2$ and $I_{\min}=(A_1-A_2)^2$.
$$\frac{I_{\max}}{I_{\min}}=\frac{(2a+a)^2}{(2a-a)^2}=9$$

questions.stem: Three identical positive charges of $2.0\ \mu\text{C}$ are fixed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $0.30$ m. Taking $k=9.0\times10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}$, find the magnitude of the net force on one charge.
questions.solution:
Each of the other charges exerts a force $F=\dfrac{kq^2}{a^2}=\dfrac{(9.0\times10^9)(2.0\times10^{-6})^2}{(0.30)^2}=0.40\,\text{N}$. The two forces are separated by $60^\circ$, so
$$F_{\text{net}}=\sqrt{F^2+F^2+2F^2\cos60^\circ}=\sqrt{3}F=0.40\sqrt{3}\,\text{N}.$$

questions.stem: A particle in SHM with angular frequency $4\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$ passes $x=0$ with speed $20\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$ and then passes $x=2.5$ cm with speed $10\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$, moving in the positive $x$ direction. What is the time between these passages?
questions.solution: At $x=0$, the speed is maximum, so $A=v_{\rm max}/\omega=20/4=5$ cm. Taking $x=A\sin(\omega t)$ for motion in the positive direction, at $x=2.5$ cm we have $\sin(\omega t)=2.5/5=1/2$, hence $\omega t=\pi/6$. Thus $\displaystyle t=\frac{\pi/6}{4}=\frac{\pi}{24}\text{ s}$."}

questions.stem: Four point masses of $1$ kg, $2$ kg, $3$ kg and $4$ kg are placed consecutively at the corners of a square of side $2$ m. What is their moment of inertia about the diagonal through the $1$ kg and $3$ kg masses?
questions.solution:
The $1$ kg and $3$ kg masses lie on the axis, so they contribute zero. The other two masses are each at perpendicular distance $r=2/\sqrt{2}$ m.
$$I=(2+4)r^2=6\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2=12\ \text{kg m}^2$$
questions.subtopic: Moment of inertia of point masses

questions.stem: A $0.40$ kg pendulum bob is released from rest with its string horizontal, as shown in the figure. For a string length of $1.25$ m and $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, what are the bob's speed and the string tension at the lowest point?
questions.solution: The vertical drop is $h=L=1.25\,\text{m}$. By conservation of energy, $$v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{2(10)(1.25)}=5\,\text{m s}^{-1}.$$ At the lowest point, $T-mg=mv^2/L$, so $T=0.40(10)+0.40(25)/1.25=12\,\text{N}$.

questions.stem: In a Young’s double-slit experiment, the two slits contribute intensities $9I_0$ and $4I_0$ at a point where their phase difference is $\frac{2\pi}{3}$. The intensity there as a fraction of the maximum possible intensity for these waves is
questions.solution:
The resultant intensity is $I=I_1+I_2+2\sqrt{I_1I_2}\cos\delta$.
$$I=9I_0+4I_0+12I_0\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=7I_0$$
The maximum intensity is $I_{\max}=(\sqrt{9I_0}+\sqrt{4I_0})^2=25I_0$.
Hence, $\dfrac{I}{I_{\max}}=\boxed{\dfrac{7}{25}}$.

questions.stem: A force $mathbf{F}=(1mathbf{i}+3mathbf{j}+2mathbf{k})$ N acts at position $mathbf{r}=(2mathbf{i}-mathbf{j}+mathbf{k})$ m relative to the origin. Find the signed component of torque along the positive direction $hat{mathbf{n}}=(mathbf{i}+2mathbf{j}+2mathbf{k})/3$.
questions.solution:
The torque is $$\boldsymbol{\tau}=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(-5\mathbf i-3\mathbf j+7\mathbf k)\,\text{N m}$.
$$$\tau_n=\boldsymbol{\tau}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}=\frac{-5-6+14}{3}=1\,\text{N$ m}$$

questions.stem: A person of mass $2$ kg stands at the rim of a turntable of moment of inertia $6$ kg m$^2$ and radius $1$ m. The system rotates at $3$ rad s$^{-1}$. If the person walks to the centre, find the new angular speed and the increase in rotational kinetic energy. Treat the person as a point mass.
questions.solution:
With no external torque, angular momentum is conserved. $I_i=6+2(1)^2=8$ and $I_f=6\,\text{kg m}^2$.
$$\omega_f=\frac{I_i\omega_i}{I_f}=\frac{8(3)}{6}=4\,\text{rad s}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta K=\frac12(6)(4^2)-\frac12(8)(3^2)=12\,\text{J}$$

questions.stem: Two cylindrical rods of the same material connect the same pair of temperatures. Rod A has length $L$ and radius $r$, while rod B has length $2L$ and radius $2r$. What is the ratio of their heat currents, $H_B/H_A$?
questions.solution:
For heat conduction, $H=\dfrac{kA\Delta T}{L}$, so for the same material and temperature difference, $H\propto \dfrac{r^2}{L}$.\\
$$\dfrac{H_B}{H_A}=\dfrac{(2r)^2/(2L)}{r^2/L}=2$$

questions.stem: An object is placed $30$ cm in front of a convex lens of focal length $15$ cm. The image distance from the lens is
questions.solution:
Using the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{v}-\dfrac{1}{u}$, with $f=15$ cm and $u=-30$ cm:
$$\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{15}-\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{30}$$
Hence, $v=30$ cm.

questions.stem: A bullet of mass $0.25$ kg embeds in a stationary block of mass $0.75$ kg hanging from a string. The combined body rises by $0.8$ m after impact, as shown in the figure. Find the bullet's speed just before impact. Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.
questions.solution:
After impact, conservation of mechanical energy gives the combined speed:
$$v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{2(10)(0.8)}=4\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$
Conservation of momentum during impact: $0.25u=(0.25+0.75)v$, hence $u=16\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: The activity measurements for a radioactive sample are shown in the figure. Assuming exponential decay, choose the pair $(T_{1/2},A_{11})$, where $T_{1/2}$ is the half-life and $A_{11}$ is the activity at $t=11$ h.
questions.solution:
For exponential decay, $A(t)=A_0(1/2)^{t/T_{1/2}}$. From $A_2=800\,\text{Bq}$ and $A_8=200\,\text{Bq}$,
$$\frac{A_8}{A_2}=\left(\frac12\right)^{6/T_{1/2}}=\frac14\;\Rightarrow\;T_{1/2}=3\,\text{h}.$$
Thus $A_{11}=200(1/2)^{3/3}=100\,\text{Bq}$.

questions.stem: The atomic masses in the $\alpha$ decay shown in the figure are given there. Taking $1\ \text{u}=931.5\ \text{MeV}/c^2$, find the $Q$-value of the decay.

A uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ rotates with angular speed $\omega$ about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod. What is the ratio of the kinetic energies of its inner and outer halves?
questions.solution:
For a rod element at distance $x$, $dK=\frac12\omega^2x^2\,dm$; since $dm=\frac ML dx$, the common factors cancel in the ratio.
$$K_{\text{inner}}:K_{\text{outer}}=\int_0^{L/2}x^2dx:\int_{L/2}^{L}x^2dx=\frac{L^3}{24}:\frac{7L^3}{24}=1:7$$

questions.stem: A train moving toward and then away from a stationary observer sounds a whistle of frequency $f$. If the train's speed is $20$ m s$^{-1}$ and the speed of sound is $340$ m s$^{-1}$, what is the ratio of the apparent frequency on approach to that on recession?
questions.solution:
For a moving source and stationary observer, $f_a=f\dfrac{v}{v-v_s}$ and $f_r=f\dfrac{v}{v+v_s}$. Thus
$$\frac{f_a}{f_r}=\frac{v+v_s}{v-v_s}=\frac{340+20}{340-20}=\frac{9}{8}.$$

questions.stem: A boat moves at $5$ m s$^{-1}$ in still water while a river flows at $3$ m s$^{-1}$. To reach the point directly opposite across a $120$ m wide river, find its heading upstream from the perpendicular to the bank and its crossing time.
questions.solution: For the boat to land directly opposite, its upstream velocity component must cancel the river flow: $5\sin\theta=3$, so $\theta=36.9^\circ$. The across-river speed is $5\cos\theta=4\,\text{m s}^{-1}$, hence $$t=\frac{120}{4}=30\,\text{s}.$$

questions.stem: A proton passes undeflected through crossed fields $E=1.6\times10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$ and $B_1=0.08\ \text{T}$, both perpendicular to its velocity. It then enters a uniform field $B_2=0.10\ \text{T}$ at $60^\circ$ to its velocity. Find its displacement magnitude after half a revolution. Take $m_p=1.6\times10^{-27}\ \text{kg}$ and $e=1.6\times10^{-19}\ \text{C}$.
questions.solution: For undeflected motion, $v=E/B_1=2.0\times10^5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. In $B_2$, the half-period is $\Delta t=\pi m_p/(eB_2)=\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{s}$; hence $d_{\parallel}=v\cos60^\circ\,\Delta t=\pi\ \text{cm}$. The perpendicular displacement is the orbit diameter, $d_{\perp}=2v\sin60^\circ/\omega=2\sqrt3\ \text{cm}$, where $\omega=eB_2/m_p$. Therefore, $d=\sqrt{d_{\parallel}^2+d_{\perp}^2}=\sqrt{\pi^2+12}\ \text{cm}$.

questions.stem: A body's velocity varies linearly between the points $(t,v)=(0,0),(2,6),(5,6),(7,-2)$, with $t$ in seconds and $v$ in m s$^{-1}$. What are its displacement from $0$ to $7$ s and its maximum speed?
questions.solution:
Displacement is the signed area under the velocity–time graph:
$$\Delta x=\frac12(2)(6)+(3)(6)+\frac{6+(-2)}{2}(2)=6+18+4=28\text{ m}.$$
The maximum speed is the greatest magnitude of velocity, $\max|v|=6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: Two blocks of masses $2$ kg and $3$ kg are connected by a light string over a smooth pulley and released from rest. How fast is the $3$ kg block moving after descending $2$ m? Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.
questions.solution:
For an Atwood machine, $a=\dfrac{(3-2)g}{3+2}=2\,\text{m s}^{-2}$. From rest, after descending $s=2\,\text{m}$,
$$v^2=2as=2(2)(2)=8 \quad\Rightarrow\quad v=2\sqrt{2}\,\text{m s}^{-1}.$$

questions.stem: A person of mass $60\ \text{kg}$ stands on a spring balance in a lift accelerating downward at $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. Taking $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, what does the balance read?
questions.solution:
For downward acceleration, the balance reads the normal force $N=m(g-a)$.
$$N=60(10-2)=480\ \text{N}$$

questions.stem: A ball is projected horizontally from a tower and lands $60$ m from its base after $3$ s. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, how far horizontally has it travelled when it is $20$ m below its launch level?
questions.solution: The horizontal speed is $v_x=\dfrac{60}{3}=20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. For a vertical drop of $20$ m, $$20=\frac12(10)t^2\Rightarrow t=2\,\text{s}.$$ Hence $x=v_xt=20(2)=40$ m.

questions.stem: In two frictionless trials, a block of mass $m$ is released from rest with a spring of constant $k$ stretched by $2x$. In the other trial, a block of mass $2m$ is released from rest with a spring of constant $4k$ stretched by $x$. Find $v_1/v_2$, the ratio of their maximum speeds.
questions.solution: By energy conservation, the maximum speed is $v_{\\rm max}=A\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$. Thus $v_1=2x\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$ and $v_2=x\sqrt{\dfrac{4k}{2m}}$. Hence $\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{2}$.

questions.stem: A bead of mass $3$ kg moves along the horizontal wire segment shown in the figure, with position $x=\left(\dfrac{t^3}{3}-2t^2+3t\right)$ m for $t\geq 0$. Which statement gives its force and when the force reverses direction?
questions.solution:
$a=\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}=2t-4\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, so $F=ma=3(2t-4)=6t-12\ \text{N}$.\\
$F=0$ at $t=2\ \text{s}$, and its sign changes there; hence the force reverses direction at $t=2\ \text{s}$.

questions.stem: A uniform wire is stretched to twice its original length without change in volume. It is connected to the same voltage source for the same time. What is the ratio of the heat produced after stretching to that produced before stretching?
questions.solution:
With volume constant, $A_1L_1=A_2L_2$; hence $L_2=2L_1$ gives $A_2=A_1/2$. Thus, $\dfrac{R_2}{R_1}=\dfrac{L_2}{L_1}\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}=4$.
At fixed voltage and time, $H=\dfrac{V^2t}{R}$, so $\dfrac{H_2}{H_1}=\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}=\boxed{\dfrac14}$.

questions.stem: The length and radius of a wire are each increased by $44\%$ and $20\%$, respectively, while its resistivity remains unchanged. What is the percentage change in its resistance?
questions.solution:
For a wire, $R=\dfrac{\rho L}{\pi r^2}$, so with unchanged resistivity, $R\propto L/r^2$.
$$\frac{R_2}{R_1}=\frac{1.44}{(1.20)^2}=1$$
Hence the percentage change in resistance is $0\%$.

questions.stem: A cell of emf $12$ V is connected to a $5\ \text{Ω}$ resistor as shown in the figure. An ideal voltmeter reads $10$ V across the resistor. Find the cell’s internal resistance.
questions.solution: The current through the resistor is $I=V/R=10/5=2\,\text{A}$. The internal voltage drop is $12-10=2\,\text{V}$, so $$r=\frac{\varepsilon-V}{I}=\frac{2}{2}=1\,\Omega.$$

questions.stem: Four identical $6\ \text{Ω}$ resistors form the arms of a Wheatstone bridge, with a $3\ \text{Ω}$ galvanometer across the middle. A $12$ V source is connected across opposite vertices of the bridge. Find the equivalent resistance and galvanometer current.
questions.solution:
By symmetry, the Wheatstone bridge is balanced, so $I_G=0$. Each branch has resistance $6+6=12\,\Omega$, and the two branches are in parallel:
$$R_{\text{eq}}=12\parallel12=6\,\Omega.$$
Thus, $R_{\text{eq}}=6\,\Omega$ and $I_G=0\,\text{A}$.

questions.stem: A $2\ \Omega$ resistor is in series with a parallel combination of $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors, across an ideal $12\ \text{V}$ battery. What are the currents through the $2\ \Omega$, $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors, respectively, and the total power dissipated?
questions.solution:
$R_{\parallel}=\dfrac{6\times3}{6+3}=2\,\Omega$, hence $R_{\text{total}}=4\,\Omega$ and $I=\dfrac{12}{4}=3\,\text{A}$.\\
The parallel pair has $V=12-(3)(2)=6\,\text{V}$, so $I_{6\Omega}=1\,\text{A}$ and $I_{3\Omega}=2\,\text{A}$.\\
$P_{\text{total}}=VI=12\times3=36\,\text{W}$.

questions.stem: Two cells of emf $2$ V and $6$ V, with internal resistances $2\ \text{Ω}$ and $6\ \text{Ω}$ respectively, are connected in parallel with like terminals joined across a $1.5\ \text{Ω}$ resistor. Find the equivalent emf and the current through the resistor.
questions.solution:
For cells in parallel with like terminals, $\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{E_1/r_1+E_2/r_2}{1/r_1+1/r_2}=\dfrac{2/2+6/6}{1/2+1/6}=3\,\text{V}$.  
The equivalent internal resistance is $r_{\text{eq}}=2\parallel6=1.5\,\Omega$.  
$$I=\frac{\varepsilon_{\text{eq}}}{r_{\text{eq}}+R}=\frac{3}{1.5+1.5}=1\,\text{A}$$

questions.stem: A capacitor initially charged to voltage $V$ is connected to an identical uncharged capacitor. What are the final common voltage and the fraction of the initial energy lost as heat in the connecting wires?
questions.solution: By charge conservation, $CV=2CV_f$, so $$V_f=\frac{V}{2}.$$ The initial energy is $U_i=\frac12CV^2$, while the final energy is $U_f=\frac12(2C)(V/2)^2=U_i/2$. Hence the fraction lost as heat is $\dfrac{U_i-U_f}{U_i}=\dfrac12$.

questions.stem: Which sequence gives the alkenes in decreasing order of stability?
questions.solution:
Alkene stability increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the double bond due to greater hyperconjugative stabilisation:
$$\text{trisubstituted} > \text{disubstituted} > \text{monosubstituted} > \text{unsubstituted}$$
Hence, $\text{2-methyl-2-butene} > \text{2-methylpropene} > \text{propene} > \text{ethene}$.

questions.stem: Which compound is used as a tranquilizer, rather than as a barbiturate hypnotic or an analgesic?
questions.solution: Diazepam is a benzodiazepine used as a tranquilizer. Phenobarbital is a barbiturate, while aspirin and ibuprofen are analgesics.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about smog:
I. Photochemical smog forms in warm, stagnant air under intense sunlight.
II. It involves photolysis of $\text{NO}_2$ and oxidation of volatile organic compounds.
III. $\text{O}_3$ and PAN are oxidants in photochemical smog, unlike the reducing classical smog.
IV. $\text{SO}_2$ and smoke are its principal characteristic components.
Which statements are correct?
questions.solution: Photochemical smog forms in warm, stagnant air under intense sunlight; it involves photolysis of $\text{NO}_2$ and oxidation of $VOCs.\nIts$ oxidants include $\text{O}_3$ and PAN, while $\text{SO}_2$ and smoke characterize classical $smog.\nThus$, statements I, II and III are correct.

questions.stem:
Consider these statements about vitamins:
I. Vitamins B and C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.
II. Deficiency of vitamin B$_1$ causes beriberi, while vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
III. Human skin can synthesise vitamin D$_3$ on exposure to ultraviolet radiation.
IV. Human cells synthesise vitamin B$_{12}$ in amounts sufficient to eliminate the need for dietary intake.
Which statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Vitamins B and C are water-soluble, while A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. Deficiencies of B$_1$ and C cause beriberi and scurvy, respectively.
Skin synthesises vitamin D$_3$ on exposure to UV radiation, but humans rely on dietary vitamin B$_{12}$, which is made by microorganisms.
Hence, statements I, II and III are correct.

questions.stem: Using signed (algebraic) electron gain enthalpy values, which ordering is incorrect?
questions.solution: For signed electron gain enthalpies, more negative values are smaller. Since $\text{Cl}(-349)<\text{F}(-328)<\text{Br}(-325)<\text{I}(-295)$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, the ascending order is $\text{Cl}<\text{F}<\text{Br}<\text{I}$. Hence (A), which places F before Cl, is the incorrect ordering.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about hydrides:
I. Ionic hydrides react with water to liberate $\text{H}_2$, with $\text{H}^-$ acting as a reducing agent.
II. For group 16 covalent hydrides, thermal stability decreases and reducing character increases down the group.
III. Interstitial hydrides are generally non-stoichiometric and retain metallic conductivity.
IV. $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is thermally more stable than $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Which statements are correct?
questions.solution: In ionic hydrides, $\mathrm{H^-}$ is oxidised by water, liberating $\mathrm{H_2}$; hence I is true. Down group 16, hydride thermal stability decreases while reducing character increases, and interstitial hydrides are generally non-stoichiometric and retain metallic conductivity; II and III are true. $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ is less thermally stable than $\mathrm{H_2O}$, so IV is false. Thus, I, II and III only.

questions.stem: The octahedral splitting shown in the figure corresponds to which complex and its spin and magnetic character?
questions.solution:
In $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$, iron is in the $+2$ oxidation state, giving a $d^6$ configuration. Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong-field ligand, the electrons pair in the lower $t_{2g}$ orbitals:
$$t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$$
All electrons are paired, so the complex is low-spin and diamagnetic.

questions.stem: Pure $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$ at $1.00$ bar reaches a total equilibrium pressure of $1.50$ bar at constant temperature and volume. Find $(\alpha,K_p)$ for $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NO}_2(g)$.
questions.solution:
At constant $T,V$, pressure is proportional to total moles; hence $P_{\rm eq}=P_0(1+\alpha)$, giving $\alpha=1.50/1.00-1=0.50$$.\nThe$ equilibrium partial pressures are $p_{\mathrm{NO_2}}=2P_0\alpha=1.00$ bar and $p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}=P_0(1-\alpha)=0.50$ bar.
$$K_p=\frac{p_{\mathrm{NO_2}}^2}{p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}}=\frac{(1.00)^2}{0.50}=2.00\ \text{bar}$$

questions.stem: For a hydrogen-like ion of nuclear charge $+Ze$, what is $E_n(\text{ion})/E_n(\text{H})$ for electrons in the same orbit $n$?
questions.solution:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $E_n=-13.6\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$, while for hydrogen, $E_n=-13.6\dfrac{1}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$.
$$\frac{E_n(\text{ion})}{E_n(\text{H})}=Z^2$$

questions.stem: A first-order decomposition has rate constant $0.231\ \text{min}^{-1}$. How long does it take for $87.5\%$ of the reactant to decompose?
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $kt=\ln\left(\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}\right)$. The fraction remaining is $1-0.875=0.125=\dfrac18$.
$$t=\frac{\ln 8}{0.231}=9.0\ \text{min}$$

questions.stem: What are the shape and hybridisation of $text{XeF}_4$?
questions.solution:
Xe has $4$ bond pairs and $2$ lone pairs, so its steric number is $6$.
$$\text{Hybridisation}=sp^3d^2$$
The electron-pair geometry is octahedral; with lone pairs opposite each other, the molecular shape is square planar.

questions.stem: Which pair is most suitable for preparing ethoxycyclopentane by Williamson synthesis?
questions.solution:
Williamson synthesis proceeds by an $S_\text{N}2$ reaction, so use the primary alkyl halide, bromoethane.
$$\mathrm{C_5H_9O^- + C_2H_5Br \longrightarrow C_5H_9OC_2H_5 + Br^-}$$
Thus, sodium cyclopentoxide and bromoethane form ethoxycyclopentane.

questions.stem: Under the same conditions, gases $X$ and $Y$ effuse through the same pinhole in equal times in volume ratio $3:2$. If $M_Y = 36$ g mol$^{-1}$, find $M_X$.
questions.solution:
By Graham’s law, the volume ratio in equal times is $\dfrac{V_X}{V_Y}=\sqrt{\dfrac{M_Y}{M_X}}$.\\
$$\dfrac{3}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{36}{M_X}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad M_X=36\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2=16\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$$

questions.stem:
The following Fischer projection represents 2,3-dibromobutane. What are the configurations at C2 and C3, respectively, and how many stereoisomers does the compound have?
$$\begin{array}{ccc} & \text{CH}_3 & \\ & | & \\ \text{Br} & {-}\text{C}{-} & \text{H} \\ & | & \\ \text{H} & {-}\text{C}{-} & \text{Br} \\ & | & \\ & \text{CH}_3 & \end{array}$$
questions.solution: At both C2 and C3, the priorities are $\mathrm{Br>C>CH_3>H}$. Since the lowest-priority group H lies on a horizontal bond in each Fischer projection, reverse the observed order: both centers are $R$. The stereoisomers are the $RR/SS$ pair and one $RS$ meso form, giving $3$ in total.

questions.stem: An fcc unit cell contains how many octahedral voids and tetrahedral voids, respectively?
questions.solution:
An fcc unit cell contains $4$ lattice atoms. The number of octahedral voids equals the number of atoms, while tetrahedral voids are twice that number:
$$N_{\text{octahedral}}=4,\qquad N_{\text{tetrahedral}}=2(4)=8.$$

questions.stem: Which substance is commonly used as a protective colloid to stabilise a lyophobic gold sol?
questions.solution: Gelatin is a lyophilic colloid that forms a protective layer around lyophobic gold particles, stabilising the sol. The given salts are electrolytes, not protective colloids.

questions.stem: For the downward transitions marked as shown in the figure, which statement about the series and emitted wavelengths is correct?

options.text: A and D are Balmer; B and C are Lyman; $\lambda_D>\lambda_A>\lambda_B>\lambda_C$.
A and D are Balmer; B and C are Lyman; $\lambda_A>\lambda_D>\lambda_B>\lambda_C$.
A and B are Balmer; C and D are Lyman; $\lambda_D>\lambda_A>\lambda_B>\lambda_C$.
A and D are Balmer; B and C are Lyman; $\lambda_D>\lambda_A>\lambda_C>\lambda_B$.

questions.solution:
Transitions ending at $n=1$ belong to the Lyman series, while those ending at $n=2$ belong to the Balmer series. Thus, A and D are Balmer, and B and C are Lyman.
$$\Delta E\propto \frac{1}{n_f^2}-\frac{1}{n_i^2},\qquad \lambda\propto\frac{1}{\Delta E}$$
The energy gaps increase in the order $D,A,B,C$, so the wavelengths decrease in that order: $\lambda_D>\lambda_A>\lambda_B>\lambda_C$.

questions.stem: At room temperature, Lucas reagent gives immediate turbidity with tertiary alcohols, turbidity after a few minutes with secondary alcohols, and no turbidity with primary alcohols. What is observed with butan-2-ol?
questions.solution: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. Secondary alcohols give turbidity after a few minutes with Lucas reagent.

questions.stem: For a cell with $n=2$, $E^\circ=0.1773$ V at $298$ K, find $(\Delta G^\circ,K)$. Take $F=96500$ C mol$^{-1}$ and $R=8.314$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
For a cell, $4\Delta G^\circ=-nFE^\circ$ and $\ln K=\dfrac{nFE^\circ}{RT}$. 
$$\Delta G^\circ=-2(96500)(0.1773)=-34.2\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1},\qquad \ln K=\frac{2(96500)(0.1773)}{(8.314)(298)}=13.81$$
Thus $K=e^{13.81}\approx1.0\times10^6$.

questions.stem: For gaseous $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($Z=24$), choose its ground-state configuration, number of unpaired electrons and spin-only moment. Use $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$.
questions.solution: Neutral Cr is $[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^5 4s^1$; removing the $4s$ electron first gives $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^4$. By Hund’s rule, $n=4$ unpaired electrons, so $$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4(6)}=4.90\ \mathrm{BM}.$$

questions.stem: Following E2 elimination with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ ($\Delta$), HBr addition, and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ substitution, what is the final product from the haloalkane shown in the figure?
questions.solution:
Alcoholic KOH and heat cause E2 elimination; HBr then adds to the alkene in Markovnikov fashion, followed by substitution with aqueous KOH.
$$ (CH_3)_2CHCH_2Br \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH},\ \Delta} (CH_3)_2C{=}CH_2 \xrightarrow{HBr} (CH_3)_3CBr \xrightarrow{\text{aq. KOH}} (CH_3)_3COH $$
The final product is 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

questions.stem: The aromatic aldehyde shown undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated alkali. After acidic work-up, which product pair is formed?
questions.solution: Cannizzaro reaction disproportionates the aldehyde: $$2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{OH}^-\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOO}^-.$$ Acidic work-up converts the carboxylate to the acid; the para-fluoro substituent is retained. Thus the products are 4-fluorobenzyl alcohol and 4-fluorobenzoic acid.

questions.stem: The alkene shown in the figure is treated with $\text{O}_3$, followed by $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Which carbonyl product is formed?
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the ring C=C: the methyl-substituted carbon forms a ketone, while the carbon bearing H forms an aldehyde.
$$\mathrm{OHC-(CH_2)_4-CO-CH_3}$$
This is 6-oxoheptanal.

questions.stem: In dilute water, assuming complete dissociation of the electrolytes, what is the increasing order of van ’t Hoff factors for glucose, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CaCl}_2$?
questions.solution: For complete dissociation, the van ’t Hoff factor equals the number of particles formed per formula unit. Glucose: $i=1$; NaCl: $i=2$; CaCl$_2$: $i=3$. Hence, $\text{glucose}<\text{NaCl}<\text{CaCl}_2$.

questions.stem: For $\text{H}_2(g)+\text{Cl}_2(g)\rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(g)$, the mean bond enthalpies are H–H $436$, Cl–Cl $243$ and H–Cl $431\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Find $\Delta H$.
questions.solution:
Using $�24H=\sum D(\text{bonds broken})-\sum D(\text{bonds formed})$,
$$\Delta H=(436+243)-2(431)=-183\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}.$$

questions.stem: At $298\ \text{K}$, $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})=426$, $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})=91$ and $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})=126$, all in $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Find $\Lambda_m^\circ$ for acetic acid.
questions.solution:
By Kohlrausch’s law of independent ionic migration,
$$\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{CH_3COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{CH_3COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{NaCl})$$
$=426+91-126=391\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: In aqueous solution, which is the decreasing order of basic strength, taking solvation and resonance into account?
questions.solution:
Alkyl groups donate electron density to nitrogen; in water, solvation gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}>\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2>\text{NH}_3$. In aniline, resonance delocalizes the lone pair, making it less available for protonation.
$$ (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}>\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2>\text{NH}_3>\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 $$

questions.stem: In the same polar protic solvent, arrange these haloalkanes in increasing order of their $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction rates: chloroethane, 2-chloropropane and benzyl chloride.
questions.solution:
The $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ rate increases with the stability of the carbocation formed in the rate-determining step.
$$\text{ethyl}^+ < \text{isopropyl}^+ < \text{benzyl}^+$$
The benzyl carbocation is resonance-stabilized; hence, chloroethane $<$ 2-chloropropane $<$ benzyl chloride.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the anomalous behaviour of nitrogen:
I. Nitrogen does not form pentahalides because its valence shell has no vacant $d$ orbitals.
II. Its small size permits effective $p\pi$–$p\pi$ overlap and favors multiple bonding.
III. Nitrogen cannot show positive oxidation states in compounds because it is more electronegative than most elements.
IV. The strong triple bond in $\text{N}_2$ contributes to the existence of elemental nitrogen mainly as diatomic molecules.
V. The $\text{N}-\text{N}$ single bond is weaker than the $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bond due to greater lone-pair repulsion, so nitrogen shows less catenation.
Which combination of statements is valid?

options.text: II, III, IV and V only
I, II, IV and V only

questions.solution: Nitrogen lacks vacant $d$ orbitals and cannot expand its octet to form pentahalides (I). Its small size favors effective $p\pi$–$p\pi$ overlap and multiple bonding (II); the strong $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ bond makes elemental nitrogen predominantly diatomic (IV). Greater lone-pair repulsion weakens the $\text{N}-\text{N}$ single bond relative to $\text{P}-\text{P}$, reducing catenation (V). Nitrogen can show positive oxidation states, so III is false; hence (D).

questions.stem: What is the correct IUPAC name of the octahedral complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$?
questions.solution:
The complex ion has charge $+1$; with neutral $\text{NH}_3$ and two $\text{Cl}^-$ ligands, $x-2=+1$, so cobalt is in the $+3$ oxidation state.
Ligands are named alphabetically: ammine before chlorido. Hence the name is tetraamminedichloridocobalt(III) chloride.

questions.stem: Which is the increasing order of average N–O bond lengths in $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_2^-$ and $\text{NO}_3^-$?
questions.solution:
Resonance gives average N–O bond orders of $2$, $1.5$, and $\frac{4}{3}$ in $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_2^-$, and $\text{NO}_3^-$, respectively. Since bond length decreases as bond order increases,
$$\text{NO}_2^+ < \text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^-$$

questions.stem: Which of the following complexes can exist as cis–trans geometrical isomers?
questions.solution: For a square-planar complex of the type $[MA_2B_2]$, identical ligands can be adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans). Thus $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ exists as cis–trans geometrical isomers; the other complexes do not.

questions.stem:
Which statements about rhombic and monoclinic sulphur are $correct?
I$. Rhombic sulphur is stable below $369\ 	ext{K}$$.
II$. Monoclinic sulphur is stable from $369\ 	ext{K}$ to its melting $point.
III$. Both allotropes contain $	ext{S}_8$ rings.
questions.solution: Rhombic sulphur is stable below the transition temperature, approximately $369\,\text{K}$; monoclinic sulphur is stable from $369\,\text{K}$ to its melting point. Both allotropes consist of puckered $\text{S}_8$ rings. Hence, I, II and III are correct.

questions.stem: On mixing $100\ \text{mL}$ of $0.10\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ with $200\ \text{mL}$ of $0.20\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ $\text{NaOH}$, what is the molarity of excess $\text{OH}^-$? Assume complete neutralisation.
questions.solution:
Complete neutralisation of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ requires $3$ mol of $\text{OH}^-$ per mole of acid.
$$n_{\text{OH}^-\!,\,\text{excess}}=(0.200)(0.20)-3(0.100)(0.10)=0.010\ \text{mol}$$
The total volume is $0.300\ \text{L}$, so $[\text{OH}^-]=0.010/0.300=3.33\times10^{-2}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: A sparingly soluble salt $\text{AB}_2$ dissociates as $\text{AB}_2(s)\rightleftharpoons\text{A}^{2+}+2\text{B}^-$. If its molar solubility in pure water is $1.0\times10^{-2}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$, what is its $K_{sp}$?
questions.solution:
For molar solubility $s$, $[\text{A}^{2+}]=s$ and $[\text{B}^-]=2s$. Thus,
$$K_{sp}=s(2s)^2=4s^3=4(1.0\times10^{-2})^3=4.0\times10^{-6}.$$

questions.stem: Which aqueous ion is colourless because its electronic configuration permits no $d$–$d$ transition?
questions.solution: A $d$–$d$ transition requires electrons in partially filled $d$ orbitals. For $\text{Sc}^{3+}$, the configuration is $[\text{Ar}]3d^0$, so no $d$–$d$ transition is possible. Thus, $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ is colourless.

questions.stem: Which property is shared by lithium and magnesium but not by the other alkali metals?

options.text: Their carbonates are thermally stable toward oxide formation.
They form stable superoxides on reaction with oxygen.
They react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides.
Their hydroxides are highly soluble in water.

questions.solution:
Lithium and magnesium react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides:
$$6\text{Li}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow2\text{Li}_3\text{N},\qquad 3\text{Mg}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$$
Among the alkali metals, only lithium shows this property.

questions.stem: Though the analyst's prose was ___—carefully weighed rather than hurried—her method was ___: she selected evidence to advance a preordained conclusion rather than test it.

Choose the best improvement for the underlined construction:

She is **capable to solve** the problem without assistance.
questions.solution: “Capable” is followed by the preposition “of” and a gerund: “capable of solving.” Thus, the correct construction is “She is capable of solving the problem without assistance.”

questions.stem:
Read the five sentences and identify the one that should open the paragraph.

A. For decades, urban planners treated stormwater as a nuisance to be channelled rapidly out of streets.
B. That approach, however, often transferred flood risk to neighbourhoods downstream.
C. In response, some cities are redesigning parks and pavements to absorb rainfall where it falls.
D. These “sponge city” measures include permeable surfaces, wetlands, and planted roofs.
E. Their benefits extend beyond flood control, since they can also cool streets and improve urban habitats.
questions.solution: Sentence A introduces the topic by describing the traditional approach to stormwater. B refers back to “that approach,” while C–E depend on the response and measures introduced later; hence A should open the paragraph.

questions.stem: The roads were blocked by fallen trees, so the rescue team had to take a ______ route to reach the village.
questions.solution: Blocked roads make the usual route unusable, so the team must take a route that is not the same as usual. “Different” fits this meaning.

questions.stem: Change into active voice: The committee was informed by the secretary that the revised schedule had been approved by the chair before the delegates arrived.

options.text: The chair informed the secretary that the committee had approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.
The secretary had informed the committee that the chair approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.
The secretary informed the committee that the chair had approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.
The secretary informed the committee that the chair has approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.

questions.solution: The passive “was informed by the secretary” becomes the active “the secretary informed.” In the subordinate clause, “had been approved by the chair” becomes “the chair had approved”; “arrived” remains unchanged. Thus, the sentence matches option (C).

questions.stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to **cautious** as used in the sentence: “The cautious driver slowed down on the slippery road.”
questions.solution: “Cautious” means taking care to avoid danger; “careful” has the nearest meaning. Hasty and reckless imply a lack of caution.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best corrects the tense error: The research team has published its findings last month after reviewing the archived records.

options.text: The research team had published its findings last month after reviewing the archived records.
The research team has published its findings last month after reviewing the archived records.
The research team published its findings last month after reviewing the archived records.
The research team publishes its findings last month after reviewing the archived records.

questions.solution: “Last month” specifies a completed time in the past, so use the simple past tense: “published.”

questions.stem: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the capitalised word: The village had a **SCARCE** supply of clean water during the drought.
questions.solution: “Scarce” means limited or insufficient; its opposite is “abundant.”

questions.stem: After the examinations, Rina had to **burn the midnight oil** to complete her project. What does the idiom mean?
questions.solution: “Burn the midnight oil” means to work or study late into the night.

questions.stem:
Arrange P, Q, R and S to complete the sentence meaningfully.

The curator displayed the painting

P. only after
Q. a laboratory test showed
R. that its pigment would not fade
S. when exposed to sunlight.
questions.solution: P begins the time clause, followed by Q’s subject and verb; R completes the test’s “that” clause, and S completes “would not fade.” The sequence is PQRS.

questions.stem: My grandfather ______ walk several kilometres to school when he was a boy.
questions.solution: “Used to” expresses a repeated past action and is followed by the base verb “walk”; hence, “My grandfather used to walk several kilometres to school.”

questions.stem: The city seemed a palimpsest: beneath its glass towers, older streets and customs remained faintly legible. Here, “palimpsest” means:

options.text: A chronological account of a community’s development
A settlement preserved in its original condition
A layered record retaining faint traces of earlier forms
An idealised recollection of a vanished way of life

questions.solution: A palimpsest is a layered record in which traces of earlier forms remain visible beneath a newer surface. Here, the city retains faint traces of its past beneath its modern towers.

questions.stem:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

On a summer afternoon, the temperature in a city can vary sharply from one street to another. Asphalt and concrete absorb solar energy and release it slowly, while buildings may restrict the movement of air. Trees help moderate this heat in two ways: their leaves provide shade, and the release of water vapour from leaves cools the surrounding air. The combined cover of branches and leaves is known as the urban tree canopy.

Planting trees, however, is not an instant solution. A newly planted sapling offers little shade, and many young trees fail to survive if they are not watered or protected during their first years. City planners therefore need to budget for care as well as planting. They can also use maps of existing canopy and temperature readings to identify neighbourhoods that have little shade and experience intense heat. Prioritising such areas may bring the greatest benefit to residents who walk, wait for buses, or work outdoors.

Tree planting must also suit local conditions. A species that grows well in one climate may need too much water in another, while roots or branches can interfere with roads and power lines. Careful selection and long-term maintenance make urban trees a more dependable part of heat planning. They cannot replace measures such as reflective roofs or well-designed public spaces, but they can complement them. The aim is not simply to count newly planted trees; it is to create lasting shade where people need it most.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Urban heat depends mainly on whether buildings restrict the movement of air.
Cities should replace reflective roofs with trees to control rising summer temperatures.
Tree planting is most effective when the same species is used across every neighbourhood.
Urban trees can reduce heat, but successful planting requires careful planning and continued care.

questions.solution: Trees cool urban areas through shade and water-vapour release, but effective planting depends on suitable locations, species selection, and continued care. They complement other heat-reduction measures.

questions.stem: Why does the passage recommend budgeting for care as well as planting?

options.text: Young trees provide little shade at first and may not survive without attention.
Mature trees need to be replaced whenever nearby roads are repaired.
Newly planted trees require more water than reflective roofs do.
Trees can cool the air only after buildings have been redesigned.

questions.solution: Saplings provide little shade initially and may not survive their first years without watering or protection. Therefore, budgets should include care as well as planting.

questions.stem: Pointing to a boy, Nita said, “He is the son of my father’s only son.” How is the boy related to Nita?
questions.solution: Nita’s father’s only son is her brother. The boy is her brother’s son, so he is Nita’s nephew.

questions.stem:
Using each letter of **INTERCHANGEABLE** at most once, how many of the following words of nine or more letters can be formed?

**Words:** breathing, charitable, celebrate, reachable, chandelier, horizontal, enlighten, integral, changeable, triangle
questions.solution: The available letters are $E^3, A^2, N^2$ and one each of $I,T,R,C,H,G,B,L$. Of the listed words with at least 9 letters, breathing, charitable, celebrate, reachable, enlighten and changeable can be formed. Chandelier needs $D$, while horizontal needs unavailable letters; integral and triangle have fewer than 9 letters. Hence the count is $6$.

questions.stem: Three of the following pairs have the same relationship. Select the odd pair.
questions.solution: Paris, Lima, and Tokyo are the capitals of France, Peru, and Japan, respectively. Australia’s capital is Canberra, not Sydney; hence (B) is the odd pair.

questions.stem: The two lines through the origin, each perpendicular to one of the lines represented by $5x^2+4xy-y^2-13x+5y-6=0$, have joint equation
questions.solution:
The slopes of the lines represented by the quadratic part satisfy $5+4m-m^2=0$, giving $m=5,-1$. Their perpendicular slopes are $-1/5,1$, so the joint equation is
$$\left(y+\frac{x}{5}\right)(y-x)=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad 5y^2-4xy-x^2=0.$$

questions.stem: The sums of the first $5$ and first $8$ terms of an arithmetic progression are $35$ and $80$, respectively. Find its $10$th term.
questions.solution:
Using $S_n=\frac n2[2a+(n-1)d]$, the given sums give
$$a+2d=7,\qquad 2a+7d=20.$$
Solving, $a=3$ and $d=2$; hence $t_{10}=a+9d=3+18=21$.

questions.stem: Find the distance between the points $(1,-2,3)$ and $(5,1,3)$ in three-dimensional space.
questions.solution:
Using the 3D distance formula,
$$d=\sqrt{(5-1)^2+(1-(-2))^2+(3-3)^2}=\sqrt{16+9}=5.$$

questions.stem: If $P(A)=\dfrac{3}{5}$, $P(B)=\dfrac{2}{5}$ and $P(A\cap B)=\dfrac{1}{5}$, find $P(A\mid B^c)$.
questions.solution: $P(A\cap B^c)=P(A)-P(A\cap B)=\frac{3}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{2}{5}$ and $P(B^c)=1-P(B)=\frac{3}{5}$. $$P(A\mid B^c)=\frac{P(A\cap B^c)}{P(B^c)}=\frac{2/5}{3/5}=\frac{2}{3}$$

questions.stem: For $f(x)=(x-2)(x+1)^2$, in which interval is $f$ strictly increasing?
questions.solution:
$$f'(x)=3(x+1)(x-1).$$
Thus $f'(x)>0$ for $x>1$, so $f$ is strictly increasing on $(2,4)$.

questions.stem: Evaluate $�displaystyle\int (\sin x+\cos x)^4(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx$.
questions.solution:
Let $u=\\sin x+\\cos x$, so $du=(\\cos x-\\sin x)\\,dx$. Then
$$\\int u^4\,du=\\frac{u^5}{5}+C=\\frac{(\\sin x+\\cos x)^5}{5}+C.$$

questions.stem: For $z=-2+3i$, evaluate $\dfrac{1}{z}+\dfrac{z}{\bar z}$ in the form $a+ib$.
questions.solution:
Since $|z|^2=13$ and $\bar z=-2-3i$,
$$\frac1z=\frac{-2-3i}{13},\qquad \frac{z}{\bar z}=\frac{(-2+3i)^2}{13}=\frac{-5-12i}{13}.$$
Hence $\displaystyle \frac1z+\frac{z}{\bar z}=\frac{-7-15i}{13}$. ∎

questions.stem: For $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$, $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec c=\hat i+\hat k$, find $[\vec a,\vec b,\vec c]$.
questions.solution:
The scalar triple product is $[\vec a,\vec b,\vec c]=\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)$.
$$\vec b\times\vec c=(\hat j+\hat k)\times(\hat i+\hat k)=\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$$
Thus $[\vec a,\vec b,\vec c]=(\hat i+\hat j)\cdot(\hat i+\hat j-\hat k)=2$.

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sin 5x-\sin 2x}{2x+\sin 3x}$.
questions.solution:
Using $\sin(kx)\sim kx$ as $x\to0$, 
$$\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin5x-\sin2x}{2x+\sin3x}=\frac{5-2}{2+3}=\frac35.$$

questions.stem: The lines $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y+2}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x-3}{2}=\dfrac{y}{1}=\dfrac{z-1}{-1}$ are
questions.solution:
The direction vectors are $�24\mathbf d_1=(1,2,1),\quad \mathbf d_2=(2,1,-1)�24$, which are not parallel. Taking points $A=(1,-2,0)$ and $B=(3,0,1)$ on the lines,
$$
(\mathbf B-\mathbf A)\cdot(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)=(2,2,1)\cdot(-3,3,-3)=-3\ne0.

questions.stem: An ellipse centred at the origin has its major axis along the $x$-axis, eccentricity $\dfrac{3}{5}$ and focus $(3,0)$. Its equation is
questions.solution:
For an ellipse, $e=\dfrac{c}{a}$. With $c=3$ and $e=\dfrac35$, we get $a=5$.
$$b^2=a^2-c^2=25-9=16$$
Hence the equation is $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$.

questions.stem: The general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1+\dfrac{y}{x}$, for $x\ne0$, is
questions.solution:
Put $y=vx$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$. Then $v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1+v$, giving $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac1x$.
$$v=\ln|x|+C\quad\Rightarrow\quad y=x(\ln|x|+C).$$

questions.stem: The foot of the perpendicular from $P(4,0,1)$ to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{1}=\dfrac{z-2}{-2}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $Q=(1+2t,-1+t,2-2t)$ be the foot. Since $PQ$ is perpendicular to the line's direction $(2,1,-2)$,
$$(Q-P)\cdot(2,1,-2)=0\Rightarrow 9t-9=0\Rightarrow t=1.$$Hence $Q=(3,0,0)$.

questions.stem: How many onto functions are there from a set of $7$ elements to a set of $4$ elements?
questions.solution: By inclusion–exclusion, the number of onto functions is $$4^7-\binom41 3^7+\binom42 2^7-\binom43 1^7=16384-8748+768-4=8400.$$

questions.stem: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\left(x^3+\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\right)\,dx$ is
questions.solution:
Since $x^3$ is odd, $[?]$ its integral over $[-1,1]$ is zero. Also,
$$\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{dx}{1+x^2}=[\arctan x]_{-1}^{1}=\frac{\pi}{4}-\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
Hence the value is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.stem: An antiderivative of $\displaystyle\int x\ln x\,dx$ is
questions.solution:
Using integration by parts, take $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=\frac{dx}{x}$ and $v=\frac{x^2}{2}$.\\
$$\int x\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac12\int x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}+C.$$

questions.stem: The sum $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{r(r+2)}$, for a positive integer $n$, is
questions.solution:
Using partial fractions,
$$\frac{1}{r(r+2)}=\frac12\left(\frac1r-\frac1{r+2}\right).$$
The sum telescopes: $S_n=\frac12\left(1+\frac12-\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{n+2}\right)=\boxed{\frac{n(3n+5)}{4(n+1)(n+2)}}$.

questions.stem: The value of $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&0\\0&3&1\\2&1&1\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.solution:
Expanding along the first row,
$$\begin{vmatrix}1&2&0\\0&3&1\\2&1&1\end{vmatrix}=1(3-1)-2(0-2)=2+4=6.$$

questions.stem: Given $\vec a=2\hat i-\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$ and $\vec c=3\hat i+2\hat k$, find $\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)$.
questions.solution:
Using $
\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b(\vec a\cdot\vec c)-\vec c(\vec a\cdot\vec b),
\quad \vec a\cdot\vec c=12,\quad \vec a\cdot\vec b=-3.$
$$\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=12(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+3(3\hat i+2\hat k)=21\hat i+24\hat j-6\hat k.$$

questions.stem: A random variable $X$ has a binomial distribution with $18$ trials and success probability $\dfrac{5}{9}$. Its mean and variance, respectively, are
questions.solution:
For a binomial distribution, $\text{mean}=np$ and $\text{variance}=npq$, where $q=1-p=\frac49$.
$$\text{Mean}=18\frac59=10,\qquad \text{Variance}=18\frac59\frac49=\frac{40}{9}$$

questions.stem: How many four-digit numbers divisible by $5$ can be formed from the digits $\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ without repetition?
questions.solution:
A number divisible by $5$ must end in $0$ or $5$.  
Last digit $0$: $5\cdot{}^4P_2=60$; last digit $5$: $4\cdot{}^4P_2=48$.  
$$60+48=108$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sin x+\cos x}$.
questions.solution:
Set $t=\tan\dfrac{x}{2}$, so $dx=\dfrac{2\,dt}{1+t^2}$, $\sin x=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$, and $\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$. The limits become $t=0$ to $1$.
$$\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+\sin x+\cos x}=\int_0^1\frac{dt}{1+t}=\ln 2.$$

questions.stem: The line $y=mx+5$, with $m>0$, touches the circle $x^2+y^2=9$. The value of $m$ is
questions.solution:
The distance from the origin to the tangent line $mx-y+5=0$ must equal the circle’s radius, $3$.
$$\frac{5}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=3 \implies m^2=\frac{16}{9}.$$
Since $m>0$, $m=\frac{4}{3}$.

questions.stem: Let $f:\mathbb R\to[1,\infty)$ and $g:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{x-1}$. Which statement is true?
questions.solution:
For $x\in[1,\infty)$,
$$
(f\circ g)(x)=\left(\sqrt{x-1}\right)^2+1=x.
$$
Thus the stated identity holds for every $x$ in the domain.

questions.stem: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(x-\dfrac{2}{x^2}\right)^9$ is
questions.solution:
The general term is $T_{r+1} = \binom{9}{r}(-2)^r x^{9-3r}$. For the term independent of $x$, set $9-3r=0$, giving $r=3$.
$$\binom{9}{3}(-2)^3 = -672$$

questions.stem: The general solution of $\sin 3\theta=\cos\theta$ is
questions.solution:
Using $\sin x=\sin y$ iff $x=y+2n\pi$ or $x=\pi-y+2n\pi$:
$$3\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta+2n\pi\quad\text{or}\quad 3\theta=\pi-\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)+2n\pi.
$$
Hence $\theta=\frac{\pi}{8}+\frac{n\pi}{2}$ or $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}+n\pi$, where $n\in\mathbb Z$.

questions.stem: How many arrangements of the letters of TRAIL have T and L nonadjacent?
questions.solution:
Total arrangements of the five distinct letters are $5!$. If T and L are adjacent, treat them as one block; the block can be ordered in $2$ ways:
$$5!-2\cdot4!=120-48=72.$$

questions.stem: If $|z-(1+2i)|=|z-(-3+4i)|$ and $|z|=5$, then the product of the possible values of $z$ is
questions.solution:
Let $z=x+iy$. The equidistance condition gives the perpendicular bisector $y=2x+5$. Using $|z|=5$:
$$x^2+(2x+5)^2=25\Rightarrow 5x(x+4)=0,$$
so $z=5i$ or $z=-4-3i$. Their product is $(5i)(-4-3i)=15-20i$.

questions.stem: If a square matrix $A$ satisfies $A^2=3A-2I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix, then $A^6$ equals
questions.solution:
$A^2=3A-2I$; multiplying successively by $A$ gives $A^5=31A-30I$.
$$A^6=31A^2-30AI=31(3A-2I)-30A=63A-62I$$

questions.stem: The equation of the circle through $(2,0)$, $(0,2)$ and $(0,0)$ is
questions.solution:
Write the circle as $x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey+F=0$. Since it passes through $(0,0)$, $F=0$; substituting $(2,0)$ and $(0,2)$ gives $D=-2$ and $E=-2$.
$$x^2+y^2-2x-2y=0$$

questions.stem: The general solution of $�\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x(1+y^2)$ is
questions.solution:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\frac{dy}{1+y^2}=2x\,dx \quad\Rightarrow\quad \tan^{-1}y=x^2+C.
$$
Hence, $y=\tan(x^2+C)$.

questions.stem: Let $A$ and $B$ be real square matrices of the same order. Which statement is always true?

options.text: If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric, then $AB$ is symmetric.
If $A$ and $B$ are skew-symmetric, then $AB$ is skew-symmetric.
For every square matrix $A$, $A-A^T$ is symmetric.

questions.solution:
Using $(AB)^T=B^TA^T$ and symmetry, $A^T=A$ and $B^T=B$.
$$ (AB)^T=B^TA^T=BA $$

questions.stem: The range of $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2+4}{x^2+2x+4}$, for $x\in\mathbb R$, is
questions.solution: Since $x^2+2x+4>0$, set $y=f(x)$ and rearrange: $$(y-1)x^2+2yx+4(y-1)=0.$$ For real $x$, its discriminant must satisfy $4(-3y^2+8y-4)\ge 0$, so $\frac{2}{3}\le y\le 2$. Both endpoints are attained, at $x=2$ and $x=-2$, respectively; hence the range is $\left[\frac{2}{3},2\right]$.

questions.stem: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability that the number obtained is divisible by $2$ or $3$?
questions.solution:
The outcomes divisible by $2$ or $3$ are $\{2,3,4,6\}$. Hence,
$$P=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}.$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\tan\left(\sin^{-1}\dfrac35+\cos^{-1}\dfrac5{13}\right)$.
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha=\sin^{-1}\frac35$ and $\beta=\cos^{-1}\frac5{13}$. Then $\tan\alpha=\frac34$ and $\tan\beta=\frac{12}{5}$.
$$\tan(\alpha+\beta)=\frac{\frac34+\frac{12}{5}}{1-\frac34\cdot\frac{12}{5}}=-\frac{63}{16}.$$

questions.stem: Given $a>0$, find $a+b$ if $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{e^{2ax}-1}{x},&x<0,\\ ax^2+b,&0\le x<1,\\ b^2-1,&x\ge1\end{cases}$ is continuous at both $x=0$ and $x=1$.
questions.solution:
At $x=0$, continuity gives $b=\lim_{x\to0^-}\frac{e^{2ax}-1}{x}=2a$. At $x=1$, it gives $a+b=b^2-1$.
Substituting $b=2a$:
$$4a^2-3a-1=(a-1)(4a+1)=0.$$
Since $a>0$, $a=1$, so $b=2$ and $a+b=3$.

questions.stem: The value of $\sin 75^\circ$ is
questions.solution:
Using $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$,
$$\sin75^\circ=\sin45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\cos45^\circ\sin30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.$$

questions.stem: The roots $\alpha,\beta$ of $x^2-kx+4=0$ satisfy $\alpha^2+\beta^2=17$. If $k>0$, find $k$.
questions.solution:
$\alpha+\beta=k$ and $\alpha\beta=4$ by Vieta’s formulas. Hence
$$\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=k^2-8=17.$$
Thus $k^2=25$; since $k>0$, $k=5$.

questions.stem: Using differentials, the approximate value of $\sqrt{25.4}$ is
questions.solution:
For $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$, $f'(x)=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$. Linearizing at $x=25$ gives
$$\sqrt{25.4}\approx 5+\frac{1}{10}(0.4)=5.04.$$

questions.stem: A data set has mean $4$ and standard deviation $2$. If each observation $x$ is replaced by $3x+1$, the new mean and standard deviation are
questions.solution: For a linear transformation $y=ax+b$, the mean becomes $a\mu+b$ and the standard deviation becomes $|a|\sigma$. Thus, $$\mu_y=3(4)+1=13,\qquad \sigma_y=|3|(2)=6.$$

questions.stem: For $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x+2$, what is the value of $f$ at its local minimum?
questions.solution:
The derivative is $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3)$, which changes from negative to positive at $x=3$; hence the local minimum occurs there.
$$f(3)=27-54+27+2=2$$

questions.stem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x+3}{x^2+2x+1}\,dx$.
questions.solution:
Factor the denominator and split the integrand:
$$\frac{x+3}{x^2+2x+1}=\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{2}{(x+1)^2}.$$
Hence, $\displaystyle\int \frac{x+3}{x^2+2x+1}\,dx=\ln|x+1|-\frac{2}{x+1}+C$.

questions.stem: The image of the point $(2,1)$ in the line $3x+4y-5=0$ is
questions.solution:
For reflection across $ax+by+c=0$, $(x',y')=(x,y)-\dfrac{2(ax+by+c)}{a^2+b^2}(a,b)$. Here $L=3(2)+4(1)-5=5$ and $a^2+b^2=25$.
$$ (x',y')=(2,1)-\frac{10}{25}(3,4)=\left(\frac45,-\frac35\right). $$

questions.stem: The domain of the real-valued function $f(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{5-2x}}{\log_3(x+1)}$ is
questions.solution: For the square root, $5-2x\geq 0$, so $x\leq \frac{5}{2}$. The logarithm requires $x+1>0$, and the denominator requires $\log_3(x+1)\ne 0$, hence $x>-1$ and $x\ne 0$. Thus the domain is $\boxed{(-1,0)\cup(0,\frac{5}{2}]}$.

questions.stem: For the curve $x^2+xy+y^2=7$, find the slope of the tangent at $(1,2)$.
questions.solution:
Implicitly differentiating $x^2+xy+y^2=7$ gives
$$2x+y+(x+2y)\frac{dy}{dx}=0,\qquad \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2x+y}{x+2y}.$$
At $(1,2)$, the slope is $-\dfrac{2+2}{1+4}=-\dfrac45$.
